about: The order a table's rows show in (manual/parts.data.md, sortable), the same on every renderer: the web's Svelte part and the Avalonia control are both run through these cases. A table has its rows in the order of the data; `order` is the table's first order (order by field [desc]), `sortable` lets a click on a header sort by that column, and a second click on it sorts the other way. Sorting changes only how the rows show: a row keeps its place in the data, so events and the chosen row name the row by that place. Text sorts ignoring case, numbers as numbers, a choice (an enum or a reference) by the label it shows; an empty value (none) comes first either way and empty text sorts as text, first going up and last going down, as a database sorts it (the user, 2026-11-21: "First, everywhere", as in comparisons and in find ... order by), and rows that are equal keep the order of the data. Steps: click a shown row (counted from the top as shown), sort by a column (a click on its header). Expected: the rows as shown, top to bottom, by their place in the data; the events ('select 2' when the row at place 2 of the data is chosen); the chosen row by its place in the data.

cases.name: without an order the rows show as the data has them
numbers sort as numbers, with an empty value first
an empty value comes first the other way too
empty text is text: last going down
a choice sorts by the label it shows
a click on a sortable header sorts by that column
a second click on the header sorts the other way
a click on another header sorts by that one, first ascending
without sortable a click on a header changes nothing
a row clicked in sorted order is chosen by its place in the data
sorting is no select and the chosen row stays chosen
